headline: Storm and thundershowers expected in Dhaka and 13 other regions, river ports warned
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has issued a warning for temporary stormy winds and thundershowers, with speeds of 45-60 km/h, affecting several districts by Monday afternoon.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has forecast stormy winds and thundershowers for Dhaka and 13 other districts across the country by Monday afternoon. River ports in the affected areas have been advised to hoist cautionary signal number 1.
This weather forecast was released for the country's internal river ports, covering the period from 5 AM to 1 PM on Monday, August 17.
The districts expected to be impacted include Rajshahi, Pabna, Dhaka, Faridpur, Jashore, Kushtia, Khulna, Barishal, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Cumilla, Chattogram, and Cox's Bazar.

Winds are anticipated to blow from the south/southeast at speeds of 45-60 km/h during these temporary stormy conditions. Residents and river transport operators in these regions are urged to remain vigilant.

headline: Retired teachers and staff finally receive overdue retirement and welfare benefits after years of waiting
summary: After years of financial uncertainty and delays, nearly 70,000 private educational institution teachers and staff are now receiving a portion of their long-awaited dues, easing widespread frustration.
details: After years of anticipation, retired teachers and staff of private educational institutions have begun receiving their long-due retirement and welfare benefits. The Non-Government Educational Institution Teacher and Employee Retirement Benefits Board and Welfare Trust have released a portion of the funds for almost all applicants.

The payment of retirement benefits has faced a severe crisis for years, with the process nearly halted during the interim government. Delays escalated after the new pay scale implementation in 2015, leading to allegations of corruption where many teachers reportedly had to pay bribes to receive their dues.

Education Minister A. N. M. Ehsanul Hoque Milon recently stated that approximately BDT 7,000 crore from teachers' retirement and welfare trust funds was embezzled during the previous Awami League government's tenure. This initiative by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is seen as a significant step to resolve the long-standing issue.

The Prime Minister inaugurated the disbursement of non-government teacher-employee retirement and welfare benefits last Saturday, with funds released to eligible applicants on the same day. Beneficiaries were informed via SMS on their mobile phones.

The Retirement Benefits Board has disbursed approximately BDT 1,550 crore as a partial payment to 70,119 teachers and staff who applied between January 2022 and July 2026. Similarly, the Welfare Trust released about BDT 647 crore for 53,477 applications.

These payments are primarily sourced from the contributions deducted from teachers' salaries during their service. Welfare benefits range from a minimum of BDT 5,000 to a maximum of BDT 316,000, while retirement benefits can go up to BDT 450,000.

While many have already received funds, some applications are pending due to incompleteness or various errors, affecting over 4,000 applicants. Officials are advising those with issues to provide necessary documents for correction.

Beneficiaries are currently receiving only a portion of their total entitlement, with the remaining amount expected to be paid later. Officials from both institutions state that special government allocation is needed for the full and swift repayment of all dues.

Funds are being sent directly to teachers' bank accounts via the 'iBAS Plus Plus' software, which verifies national ID and bank account information. Minor errors in applications can prevent payment, but funds will be resent once corrections are made.
